title: The structure sheaf of a countably indexed affine formal algebraic space has no higher cohomology
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter formal-spaces.tex (Formal Algebraic Spaces)

difficulty_reason: For a countably indexed affine formal algebraic space X the lemma asserts that the higher cohomology of the structure sheaf on the small etale site vanishes (statement lines 7764-7768). The proof first reduces the site to the affine etale site and, since finite disjoint unions are available, applies the Cech vanishing criterion to reduce the claim to the exactness of the Cech complex of a covering by a single arrow, which for the base object one writes out explicitly in terms of the values of the structure sheaf on the reductions of the iterated fibre products; the general member of the site is then dismissed as being treated in exactly the same way (proof lines 7770-7788). The computation of those values is the second step: writing X as the formal spectrum of a weakly admissible topological ring with a countable fundamental system of weak ideals of definition, the objects of the site correspond to etale algebras over it, the values of the structure sheaf are their completions, and the values on iterated fibre products are the completions of the corresponding tensor powers (proof lines 7790-7807). The third step supplies the input for exactness: the morphism from the base to the cover is faithfully flat because the cover is a covering, so the complex before completion is not merely exact but universally exact, by the descent lemma identifying that notion (proof lines 7808-7813). The fourth and last step transfers exactness through completion: the complex is split into short exact sequences, universal exactness gives that each submodule meets every ideal of the base in the image of the intersection, so the two topologies on the submodules agree, and the countable fundamental system of ideals of definition makes the completed short exact sequences exact (proof lines 7814-7838). The claim is H3: the reduction to a single-arrow Cech complex, the identification of the values of the structure sheaf as completions of tensor powers, the use of universal exactness, and the comparison of topologies through a countable system are four independent pieces of work rather than one.
